intro: Good evening from Coldwater and welcome to CLUSTER PUCK. I'm Tug Brennan, and nobody made me do this.
CPhL hockey tonight, brought to you by whoever is still paying, and I have been told not to name them on air.
Evening. Tug Brennan with you. The scheduler says these two are playing, so these two are playing.
Welcome in. The ice is down, the lights are on, and the insurance has lapsed. Let's go.

{away} at {home}. Somebody's night gets worse in the next hour.

ot.intro: Level after sixty. SUDDEN DEATH, and in this league that isn't a figure of speech.
We go to overtime. First goal wins it. So does the first body.
Sixty minutes settled nothing, so now we find out the other way.
outro: That's CLUSTER PUCK. I'm Tug Brennan. Mind how you go, and mind what's on the ice.
For the CPhL, I'm Tug Brennan. There's another one tomorrow, because there's always another one.
Tug Brennan, saying goodnight from Coldwater. Nobody won anything permanent.

Good evening from Coldwater. These two clubs can't stand each other, and the officials have been told to keep their whistles handy.
Welcome in. When these two meet, the penalty minutes run about half again what they do on any other night.

chatter.district: When the Goons are in, the cloakroom keeps a gun rack. Coats and firearms, same counter, same attendant, one ticket.
The Goons' end doesn't cheer. It gets quieter, and every other club in this league will tell you that's worse.
The Goons' bus comes down from District 9 and parks outside the front with its engine running.
Most of the Goons carry a badge on a weekday. The rest handed theirs in, or had it taken off them.
The Goons lift in the Precinct 9 gym after the night shift. The prisoners get the bench back in the morning.
Nobody's ever pressed charges over a Goons hit. Nobody's sure who they'd press them with.
chatter.westside: The Warlords practise under the Glasshouse on the coldest ice in the city. They say this is slush, and they're right.
Warlords season tickets are inherited. There's a waiting list, and it's mostly lawyers. They sit together, by the heaters.
The Warlords bring their own string quartet. Same four players for eleven years. They wear earplugs for the third period.
chatter.boomtown: The Bulldogs train in an old foundry in Boomtown. Some nights their sweaters still smell of the casting sand.
The Bulldogs bring the anvil with them. A man in an apron hits it once before the drop and their whole end goes quiet.
Bulldogs fans hang a length of pipe from the old works over the rail at their end. It rings when somebody goes into the boards under it.
chatter.marquee: The Marauders practise in a rink that shares a wall with a nightclub on the Marquee. They say they don't hear the bass any more.
Half the Marauders' end came out in costume for something else on the Marquee. They stay for the fights.
The Marauders' banner used to be a cinema sign. Two of its letters have been missing for forty years.
chatter.coldwater: The Highlanders walk out to a piper. He isn't good. He's played every one of their games for fourteen years.
Marrow Street pulls its shutters down an hour before a Highlanders game. Everybody on it is in here.
The Highlanders' sweaters are woven on a loom above a chip shop on Marrow Street. It's a real clan sett, the Malcolm.
That's Ken Raven on the Zamboni. Marrow Street boy, big Highlanders fan.
chatter.st: The Guillotines are Father Jerome's club. He blesses the ice before the drop, and the ice crew here waits until he's done.
Two of the parish men bring a pew from St Garneau's for the Guillotines' bench, on a handcart, every game.
Every Guillotines sweater goes through the Sisters of St Garneau's laundry on a Monday. The stains mostly come out.
Father Jerome never misses a Guillotines game. He sits by the door, and he watches it more than the ice.
chatter.waterfront: The Rats' end came straight off a shift at the cranes, and half of them are still in their hard hats. The hats aren't for the hockey.
The Rats practise on a pond at the Docks that floods twice a winter. There's a line on the boathouse wall showing how high, and it's above my head.
The Wharf Rats' supporters' club counts the rats under these stands as members. On a quiet night they outnumber the crowd.
Somebody throws a fish on the ice after every Rats goal. Nobody has ever seen who. The fish is always fresh.
Rats fans come in off the Docks on the late tram and call it an away trip. It's four stops.
chatter.yard: The Birds practise in a cold store in the Yards with seats bolted in. They say this ice is warm.
Birds fans brought a tannoy out of a freight shed once. Security took it off them, and in the second intermission they still shout bay numbers.
Birds fans crow when their side scores. All of them at once, and it goes on longer than you'd think.
Somebody gets a live rooster into the Gardens whenever the Birds play. Security has stopped asking how, and nobody has caught the rooster.
